hook: Four researchers at Australia's CSIRO science agency just independently confirmed the M87 black hole shadow.

sections.voiceover: Four researchers at Australia's CSIRO science agency just independently confirmed the M87 black hole shadow.
sections.visual_cue: Close up on the M87 black hole event horizon image, pulsing slightly.
b_roll: Event Horizon Telescope M87 iconic image

sections.voiceover: On November 12, 2026, CSIRO scientists verified the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of M87. How did they achieve such precision?
sections.visual_cue: Timeline graphic showing 2019 and 2026 dates, followed by a wide shot of the M87 galaxy.
b_roll: CSIRO logo and research facility footage

sections.voiceover: But they didn't just verify data; they created GenDIReCT, a powerful new image reconstruction technique.
sections.visual_cue: Abstract geometric visualization of light patterns shifting into a circular shadow.

sections.voiceover: This GenDIReCT analysis confirms the M87 shadow shape matches the original 2019 telescope models.
sections.visual_cue: Portraits of the four researchers appearing in a grid, followed by a comparison of the 2019 and 2026 images.

sections.voiceover: CSIRO scientists are bringing the M87 black hole into sharper focus with GenDIReCT.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from the black hole shadow into the vast starry expanse of space.
